stories.title: Scaffold the cargo workspace
stories.context: Create the workspace and the 8 crates from docs/architecture/TECH_STACK.md with empty libs, workspace lints and toolchain files.

acceptance.text: All 8 crates exist under crates/ with `[lints] workspace = true`
`cargo build --workspace` succeeds on the dev machine
Each crate has a `//!` doc stating its role and boundaries
Cargo.lock committed
Tests added; `just check` passes; docs updated if structure changed

stories.plan:
- **Workspace:** root `Cargo.toml` from TECH_STACK.md (resolver 3, edition 2024, workspace lints, profiles).
  Third-party versions sit in `[workspace.dependencies]` but no crate uses them yet, so `Cargo.lock` stays tiny.
- **Crates:** `leaf-core`, `leaf-model`, `leaf-editor`, `leaf-store`, `leaf-export`, `leaf-search`, `leaf-ui` (libs)
  and `leaf-app` (binary). Each has `[lints] workspace = true` and a `//!` doc stating role, boundaries and phase.
  No inter-crate dependencies yet: adding unused ones would fail `cargo machete`. Each story wires what it needs.
- **clippy.toml:** allow `unwrap`/`expect` in tests, matching CLAUDE.md.
- **Test:** `crates/leaf-app/tests/architecture.rs` reads each core crate's `Cargo.toml` and fails if it mentions
  `gpui` or `leaf-ui`, so architecture rule 1 is enforced from day one. Std only, no new deps.
- **Docs:** `docs/README.md` gains a pointer to `crates/`. ARCHITECTURE.md itself is E00-S03.
- **Risks:** Rust is not yet installed on the dev machine, so build, `Cargo.lock` and `just check` wait for it.
  Coverage of empty crates and CI wiring are E00-S02; the toolchain pin waits until the first green build.

stories.plan:
CI already ran green on `main` after E00-S01 (all 8 jobs, three OSes), so this story proves the gates bite and closes gaps.

- **Coverage gate:** add an uncovered function to a core crate locally, confirm `just cov` fails below 90%, revert.
- **Backlog job:** confirm `backlog.py --check` fails on a stale `backlog.json` and on an invalid story file.
- **Toolchain pin:** pin `rust-toolchain.toml` to 1.99.1 (the version that first built green) so CI and dev machines
  match; CI's setup action reads this file.
- **Review `ci.yml`** against the justfile so CI runs the same checks as `just check`; fix any drift.
- **Docs:** note the pin and how to bump it in `docs/architecture/TECH_STACK.md`.
- **Risks:** none known; the PR's own CI run is the final proof on all three OSes.

stories.title: Workspace doc wrapper and read API
stories.context: Type that owns the workspace LoroDoc and exposes read queries over the page tree.

acceptance.text: Create new / load from bytes / export bytes
List root pages and children of a page in order
Get page meta (title, icon, created_at, trashed_at)
Find page by PageId in O(1) via an index map
Tests added; `just check` passes; docs updated if structure changed

stories.plan:
- `leaf-model/src/workspace.rs`: `Workspace` owns the workspace `LoroDoc` and its `"pages"` tree (fractional
  index on). `new`, `from_bytes` (import a snapshot), `to_bytes` (export a snapshot).
- Read API: `root_pages`, `children(PageId)`, `page(PageId) -> PageMeta`, `contains`. All by `PageId`; Loro
  `TreeID`s stay private (ADR 0006 pattern). Trashed pages are listed too, with `trashed_at` set: hiding them
  is the trash story's job (E01-S05).
- `PageId → TreeID` index (`HashMap`), rebuilt on load. Undo will rebuild it too (E01-S06).
- `page_meta.rs`: `PageMeta` and the meta key names. `error.rs`: `ModelError` (unknown page, invalid page data,
  Loro errors).
- Loading is strict: a page without a valid `id` fails to load with a clear error, rather than being hidden.
- Tests build workspaces through raw Loro writes in test code, since the page commands arrive in E01-S03.
- Risk: none known. Loro builds for wasm32 as-is (checked).

stories.title: Page commands: create, rename, icon
stories.context: First page commands through the Command enum, each one commit.

acceptance.text: CreatePage at parent+index returns PageId
RenamePage and SetPageIcon
Each command is exactly one Loro commit
Unit tests for each command
Tests added; `just check` passes; docs updated if structure changed

stories.plan:
- `leaf-model/src/command.rs`: `WorkspaceCommand` enum (`CreatePage`, `RenamePage`, `SetPageIcon`, more in
  E01-S04/S05) and `Outcome` (`PageCreated(PageId)` or `Changed`). `Workspace::apply` is the only write path.
- Each `apply` validates first, then writes, then calls `commit()` once, so a rejected command leaves no
  half-written changes and every command is one undo step later (E01-S06).
- `CreatePage { parent, index, title, created_at }`: the model mints the `PageId` and returns it. The caller
  supplies `created_at` (Unix ms): reading the clock panics on wasm32, and tests stay deterministic.
- `SetPageIcon { page, icon: Option<String> }`: `None` clears it. An empty string is rejected. Whether the text
  is a single emoji is left to the emoji picker, since the spec says only "optional emoji icon".
- New errors: index out of range, empty icon.
- Tests: each command, each error, rejected commands write nothing, one commit per command (counted with
  `subscribe_local_update`), reload after commands. Update BLOCK_MODEL.md's command list.

stories.title: Page commands: move and reorder
stories.context: Move pages within and across parents.

acceptance.text: MovePage to new parent and index
Moving a page into its own descendant returns an error
Order preserved after reload
Unit + property tests
Tests added; `just check` passes; docs updated if structure changed

stories.plan:
- `WorkspaceCommand::MovePage { page, new_parent: Option<PageId>, index }`: one commit, validate first.
- Index meaning: the page's **final position** among the new parent's children, counted without the page
  itself. So "move to 0" always makes it first, and moving within the same parent works as drag-and-drop expects.
  Valid range is `0..=len`, where `len` excludes the page.
- Errors: unknown page or parent; `new_parent` is the page itself or one of its descendants (found by walking up
  from `new_parent`; new `MoveIntoOwnSubtree` error); index out of range. Moving to the same place is allowed.
- Tests: unit tests for each case, and order after save and load. A `proptest` property runs random create/move
  sequences, valid and invalid, against a simple reference model: same accept/reject decisions, same order
  under every parent after each step, and the same order again after reload. This also pins down Loro's index
  behaviour.
- `proptest` (already in TECH_STACK.md) added as a dev-dependency of `leaf-model`.

stories.title: Trash, restore, permanent delete
stories.context: Soft delete via trashed_at; subtree hidden from normal queries.

acceptance.text: TrashPage hides the subtree from list queries
Trash query lists trashed roots
RestorePage restores to the original parent or root if parent is gone
DeletePagePermanently removes subtree and reports page ids to delete from storage
Tests added; `just check` passes; docs updated if structure changed

stories.plan:
Done with E01-S06 on one branch (owner request). New module `workspace/trash.rs`.
- `TrashPage { page, at }` sets `trashed_at` (the caller supplies the time). The page stays in place, so its
  original parent is remembered. "In the trash" means the page or any ancestor has `trashed_at`.
- `root_pages` and `children` skip pages with `trashed_at`, so a trashed subtree disappears from listings.
  New `trash()` lists every page trashed on its own, most recent first.
- `RestorePage { page }` clears `trashed_at`. If an ancestor is still in the trash (the parent is "gone"), it
  also moves the page to the end of the top level, so it doesn't stay invisible.
- `DeletePagePermanently { page }` works only on pages in the trash. It deletes the subtree and returns
  `Outcome::PagesDeleted(ids)` so storage can drop their page docs (E03).
- Rules: no creating or moving into the trash, and a page in the trash can't be moved (restore it first).
  New errors `PageInTrash` and `NotInTrash`. Rename and icon still work in the trash.
- Tests: each command and rule, hidden subtrees, restore when the parent is gone, the deleted-ID list.

stories.title: Workspace undo/redo
stories.context: UndoManager for the workspace doc.

acceptance.text: Every page command undoes and redoes exactly
Property test: random page commands then full undo returns initial state
Tests added; `just check` passes; docs updated if structure changed

stories.plan:
- `Workspace` owns a Loro `UndoManager`, created after load so loaded history is not undoable.
  `undo()` / `redo()` return whether anything changed. Commits within the merge interval form one step; the
  default is 500 ms, as BLOCK_MODEL.md says (typing a title), and `set_undo_merge_interval` changes it (tests use 0).
- After every undo or redo, rebuild the `PageId ↔ TreeID` index: Loro re-creates nodes under new TreeIDs (ADR 0006).
- "Exact" is compared by `PageId`, order, and meta, ignoring TreeIDs (invariant 7 as reworded).
- Tests: undo and redo of every command type. Property test: random page commands (create, move, rename, icon,
  trash, restore, delete), recording the outline after each step; undo step by step must match each recorded
  outline back to the start, and redo all the way must reach the final one.

acceptance.text: BlockKind enum matches docs/architecture/BLOCK_MODEL.md

stories.title: Insert, delete and move blocks
stories.context: Structural block commands.

acceptance.text: InsertBlock at parent+index with kind and initial text
DeleteBlocks removes whole subtrees
MoveBlocks keeps relative order of the moved set
Children rules enforced (e.g. no children under heading)
Tests added; `just check` passes; docs updated if structure changed

stories.plan:
- `PageCommand` (`InsertBlock`, `DeleteBlocks`, `MoveBlocks`) applied with `PageDoc::apply`, the same pattern as
  the workspace: validate everything first, write, commit once; `Unchanged` when nothing was recorded.
- `InsertBlock { parent, index, kind, text }` mints and returns the `BlockId`. The text container is created
  with `ensure_mergeable_text`, only for kinds that have text; text on a divider is an error.
- `DeleteBlocks { ids }` removes whole subtrees and returns every deleted `BlockId` (parents first). Ids already
  inside another deleted block are fine. An empty list is `Unchanged`.
- `MoveBlocks { ids, new_parent, index }`: the moved set keeps **document order**; blocks inside another moved
  block travel with it. `index` counts the destination's children without the moved blocks. Placed as: first
  block before the sibling at `index` (or after the last), the rest each after the previous one.
- Children rules: no inserting or moving under heading, code, divider, image or unknown blocks; no moving a
  block into itself or its own descendants.
- Tests: each command and rule. A proptest runs random insert/delete/move sequences against a reference model:
  same accept/reject, same structure after every step and after reload.

stories.title: Text and mark commands
stories.context: InsertText, DeleteText, SetMark, RemoveMark.

acceptance.text: Unicode-safe offsets (tests with emoji and Indic scripts)
Marks follow the expand table in docs/architecture/BLOCK_MODEL.md
Code blocks reject marks
Link mark stores href
Tests added; `just check` passes; docs updated if structure changed

stories.plan:
Done with E02-S06 on one branch (owner request).
- `PageCommand::InsertText { id, pos, text }`, `DeleteText { id, range }`: positions are Unicode scalar offsets
  (BLOCK_MODEL.md), checked against the text length; the editor converts to graphemes (E04). Empty insert or
  empty range: `Unchanged`. Blocks without text (dividers, unknown) are rejected.
- `SetMark { id, range, mark: Mark }` / `RemoveMark { id, range, kind: MarkKind }`: `Mark` = bold, italic,
  strike, code, `Link(href)`; expand rules come from the configured table. Code blocks reject marks; empty
  link href is rejected. New errors: `TextOutOfRange`, `MarksNotAllowed`, `EmptyLink`.
- Tests: emoji with skin tone and Devanagari conjuncts at every offset; expand behaviour per mark; code block
  rejection; link href read back. A proptest compares random inserts/deletes of mixed scripts against a
  `Vec<char>` reference.

stories.title: Change block kind and props
stories.context: SetBlockKind and SetProp honouring schema rules.

acceptance.text: Text kept when the target type has text
Converting to a type without children moves children out to siblings
Converting to code strips marks
heading level validated 1..=3
Tests added; `just check` passes; docs updated if structure changed

stories.plan:
New module `page_doc/kind_ops.rs`.
- `PageCommand::SetBlockKind { id, kind }`, validated like inserts: no unknown kinds, heading level 1–3. Blocks of an
  unknown kind can't be converted, because that would rewrite them.
- **Text:** kept when the target has text; an empty container is created when converting a divider into a text
  type. Converting to a divider needs empty text: otherwise it's refused (`TextNotAllowed`) rather than losing
  words. The text container is removed so invariant 2 holds.
- **Code:** every mark is stripped from the text, unknown ones included (invariant 5).
- **Children:** converting to a kind that can't hold children moves them out to sit right after the block, in order.
- **Props:** new props are written. Known props the new kind doesn't use are removed (a heading's level when it
  becomes a paragraph); props written by a newer version are kept.
- `PageCommand::SetProp { id, prop: BlockProp }` with a typed `BlockProp` (`Checked`, `HeadingLevel`, `Language`,
  `ImageWidth`, `ImageAlt`), checked against the block's kind (`PropNotForKind`).
- Same kind or value: `Unchanged`.
- Tests: every rule above, plus round trips such as paragraph → heading → code → paragraph.

stories.title: Split and merge blocks
stories.context: SplitBlock (Enter) and MergeIntoPrevious (Backspace) model semantics.

acceptance.text: Split keeps marks on both halves
Split type rules per PRODUCT_SPEC Editor behaviour
Merge appends text and moves children to the previous block
Merge onto divider/image is rejected with a typed error the editor can handle
Tests added; `just check` passes; docs updated if structure changed

stories.plan:
New module `page_doc/split_merge.rs`.
- **`SplitBlock { id, pos }`** (Enter mid-text) returns `BlockCreated(new)`. The text after `pos` moves to the
  new block **with its marks** (`slice_delta` then `apply_delta`, so marks from newer versions survive too).
  - New kind per the spec: lists and to-dos continue (an unticked to-do); everything else becomes a paragraph.
  - Placement: right after the block, or as its **first child** if it has children, so reading order never changes.
  - Blocks without text are refused.
- **`MergeIntoPrevious { id }`** (Backspace at start) appends the block's text, with marks, to the previous
  block **in reading order**, then deletes it. It returns `BlockMerged { into, at }` so the editor can put the
  cursor at the join.
  - Children move to the previous block: at the block's old position if the previous block is its parent,
    otherwise at the end. If the previous block can't hold children (heading, code), they move up to the
    block's own position instead.
  - Merging into code strips marks (invariant 5). With no previous block: `Unchanged`.
- **Refused:** merging into a divider, image or unknown block gives a typed `MergeTargetNotText { target }`, so
  the editor can select that block instead (spec).
- **Interim editor:** Enter splits at the input's cursor; Backspace at the start of a non-paragraph turns it into
  a paragraph; at the start of a paragraph it merges into the block above, landing the cursor at the join.
- **Tests:** each rule plus mark preservation on both sides; extend the block-text proptest with split/merge
  against a reference.

stories.title: Indent and outdent
stories.context: Tab and Shift+Tab structural moves.

acceptance.text: Indent makes block the last child of previous sibling
Outdent moves block after its parent, following siblings become its children (Notion behaviour)
No-op cases return Ok without a commit
Works for multi-block selections
Tests added; `just check` passes; docs updated if structure changed

stories.plan:
- `PageCommand::Indent { ids }` / `Outdent { ids }`, applied to the outermost listed blocks one by one in
  reading order (gives Notion's result for consecutive selections).
- Indent: block becomes the last child of its previous sibling. Skipped when there is no previous sibling or it
  can't hold children (heading, code, divider, image, unknown).
- Outdent: block moves right after its parent; its following siblings become its last children, in order.
  Skipped at the top level, or when the block can't hold children but has following siblings (moving them
  elsewhere would reorder the text).
- A command where every block is skipped writes nothing and returns `Unchanged`.
- Tests: each rule and skip; multi-block indent/outdent; no commit on no-ops. Extend the block-tree proptest
  reference model with indent/outdent.

stories.title: Page undo/redo with cursor metadata

stories.plan:
New module `page_doc/undo.rs`, mirroring the workspace's undo (E01-S06).
- `PageDoc` owns a Loro `UndoManager`, created after load so saved history isn't undoable. It uses the same
  500 ms merge interval (typing groups into one step), and `set_undo_merge_interval` changes it.
- After every undo or redo, the `BlockId ↔ TreeID` index is rebuilt, because Loro re-creates nodes (ADR 0006).
- **Cursor metadata:** `Caret { block, at }` moves from `leaf-editor` into `leaf-model`, and the editor
  re-exports it. The editor tells the page its caret with `set_caret` before each command, undo or redo.
  - Loro's `on_push` hook stores that caret in the step's metadata, as a block ID plus position. Loro's own
    cursors point at TreeIDs that change on undo.
  - `on_pop` hands it back. `undo()`/`redo()` return `History::Done { caret }` or `History::Nothing`.
  - When Loro merges quick commits, it keeps the **first** step's metadata, so undoing a typing burst restores
    the caret from before the burst. For redo, the caret recorded is the one at the moment undo was pressed.
- **Tests:**
  - every block command undoes and redoes exactly (outline by `BlockId`, kinds, formatted text);
  - typing merges within the interval;
  - the caret comes back on undo and redo;
  - loaded history isn't undoable.
- **Property test (invariant 7):** extend `tests/page_invariants.rs`. Record the outline after every accepted
  command, undo step by step matching each outline back to empty, then redo to the end, calling
  `check_invariants()` after every undo and redo.
- **Scope:** wiring Cmd+Z into the editor is E04-S08.

stories.plan:
Decision only, no model code (E02-S01 builds on it).

- Scheme: each block's meta holds a permanent `id` (UUID v7 string), the same pattern pages already use.
  `BlockId` becomes a UUID newtype in `leaf-core`; `TreeID` stays an internal handle inside `leaf-model`,
  which keeps a `BlockId → TreeID` index and rebuilds it after undo, redo and import.
- ADR 0006 with alternatives (soft delete, remapping on undo, our own undo).
- BLOCK_MODEL.md: diagram, IDs table, page doc meta, commands note, invariants (new 8: unique ids; 7 reworded).
- E01-S01 context updated to the new `BlockId`. Proof: the E00-S05 spike tests already show a meta `id`
  survives every undo/redo cycle; `just check` covers the docs.

stories.plan:
- **`leaf-editor/src/page_editor.rs`:** `PageEditor` wraps a `PageDoc`.
  - `rows()` is the view model: blocks in reading order with depth, a `BlockStyle` (numbered items get their
    number here, never stored), and plain text.
  - Actions: `ensure_block` (empty page → one paragraph), `set_text` (diffs old and new text into minimal
    Delete/InsertText at Unicode positions), `enter`, `backspace_empty`, `indent`, `outdent`, `turn_into`,
    `toggle_checked`, `previous`/`next`. Unit tests for each.
- **`WorkspaceEditor`:** keeps one `PageEditor` per page, created when the page is first opened.
- **`leaf-ui` (`shell/blocks.rs`):**
  - One borderless `InputState` per block, kept in a map and refreshed from the model each frame. Typing →
    `set_text`.
  - Keys are intercepted in the capture phase on the page area: `Enter`, `Backspace` (only when empty),
    `IndentInline`/`OutdentInline` (Tab/Shift+Tab), and `MoveUp`/`MoveDown` between blocks, then stopped so the
    input doesn't also handle them.
  - Per-kind styling: heading sizes, `•` and `N.`, a `Checkbox` for to-dos, a quote bar, a monospace font for code,
    a line for dividers, placeholders for image and unknown blocks. A turn-into toolbar acts on the focused block.
- **Interim limits:** Enter always adds a block below (splitting text is E02-S05/E04-S05). Backspace only deletes
  empty, childless blocks. No inline formatting editing. The rich text element (E07-S02) replaces the inputs.
- **Checks:** GPUI tests for typing, Enter and Tab through the shell; run the app and screenshot several kinds.
